as_told.title: Modern muon detection of a big void by the Grand Gallery, and how muon scanning can fail

plain: Inside the Great Pyramid of Giza in Egypt is a long, tall sloping passage called the Grand Gallery, and in the 2020s a research team called ScanPyramids used muon detectors, which read tiny particles from space that pass through stone, to report a large hidden space they named the Big Void. A researcher named Filippo, speaking on Jesse Michels' podcast, says the team may have been confused, and that what they saw could be the floor or roof of the Grand Gallery itself, though at another point he describes the void as running parallel to the gallery. If he is right, the famous hidden chamber might not be a new room at all.
